units.title: Algorithm Analysis
units.lesson: Algorithm analysis estimates how an algorithm's resource use grows with input size. Big-O describes an upper growth bound, while Omega describes a lower bound and Theta describes a tight bound. Compare algorithms by counting dominant operations rather than relying only on machine run time.
questions: Why do we ignore constant factors in asymptotic analysis?

units.title: Linear Data Structures
units.lesson: Linear data structures arrange elements in a sequence. Arrays provide indexed access, linked lists connect nodes through references, stacks follow last-in-first-out order, and queues follow first-in-first-out order.
questions: When might a linked list be preferred over an array?

units.title: Trees and Graphs
units.lesson: Trees represent hierarchical relationships. A binary tree has at most two children per node. Common traversals include preorder, inorder and postorder. Graphs model general relationships using vertices and edges.
questions: What is the difference between a tree and a graph?

units.title: Database Fundamentals
units.lesson: A database is an organized collection of related data. A DBMS provides controlled ways to define, store, query and protect that data. Data independence separates applications from details of physical storage or logical schema changes.
questions: Differentiate logical and physical data independence.
State two advantages of a DBMS.

units.title: Relational Model and SQL
units.lesson: The relational model stores data in relations (tables). Rows are tuples and columns are attributes. Keys identify rows and connect tables. SQL defines schemas, inserts and updates data, and retrieves information using queries and joins.

units.title: Normalization and Transactions
units.lesson: Normalization organizes relations to reduce unwanted redundancy and update anomalies. Transactions are logical units of work. ACID means atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.

units.title: OS Fundamentals and Processes
units.lesson: An operating system manages hardware resources and provides services to programs. A process is a program in execution. Its state may be new, ready, running, waiting or terminated. A process control block stores information needed to manage it.
questions: List four major functions of an operating system.
What is a process control block?
Differentiate a process and a thread.

units.title: CPU Scheduling and Synchronization
units.lesson: CPU scheduling selects a ready process for execution. FCFS uses arrival order, SJF selects the shortest estimated job, and Round Robin gives each process a time quantum. Synchronization coordinates shared-resource access to avoid race conditions.
questions: How does Round Robin scheduling work?

units.title: Deadlocks and Memory Management
units.lesson: A deadlock is a situation where processes wait indefinitely for resources held by one another. The four necessary conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages and frames; virtual memory lets processes use an address space larger than physical RAM.
questions: Name the four necessary deadlock conditions.
What is the purpose of virtual memory?
